---
title: Retained source evidence
description: Keep exact historical source associations across native continuation, with fresh access checks and bounded stored-value reads.
---

A later question may need a source result that conversation trimming has removed.
Mount retained source evidence when your producer can declare the exact subject,
operation, scope and permitted fields. Payloads stay in your existing artifact
store; the native checkpoint carries only a bounded list of receipt references.

## Declare the producer's association

`withSourceEvidence` accepts a `SourceEvidenceDescriptor` and annotates a tool
without wrapping its execution. Its `SourceEvidenceDeclaration` names a typed
`SourceEvidenceSubject`, operation and `SourceEvidenceScope`; a scope contains
only governed `SourceEvidenceScalar` values. Native delivery
considers the final governed model result after placement and size limits. A
denied, failed, pending or truncated result does not become a retained source.
Direct execution outside the native Agent cannot mint an accepted observation.

<CodeFile path="examples/artifacts/retained-source-evidence.ts" region="declare-source" title="Explicit synthetic source and permitted fields" />

Static dataset declarations are explicit authorization to inspect selected stored
fields at capture; a served artifact reference alone grants nothing. Invalid
static configuration throws when the tool is declared. Returned dataset fields
must be an exact subset of a successful static declaration. The trusted producer
owns domain relationships: matching bytes does not certify that an association
is correct.

A `SourceEvidenceDatasetDeclaration` governs the capture-time selected fields.
Its detached `SourceEvidenceSource` contains only those fields and retained-rowset
limits. A returned `SourceEvidenceDataset` binds a permitted subset to the exact
native publication.

## Mount fresh admission and continue

The mount's `SourceEvidenceOptions` requires an artifact store and a trusted host
`admit` callback. Every
find, receipt read and dataset page repeats current native capability checks and
host admission. The callback may withhold an observation or narrow its scalars
and dataset fields; it cannot change the subject, scope, operation or native
status/coverage/period. Check current source permissions and privacy here, rather
than relying on a same-conversation artifact scope. The library does not replay
the original argument-dependent execution policy or tool middleware.

The callback receives a `SourceEvidenceCandidate` and returns its permitted
`SourceEvidenceProjection`. A native `SourceEvidenceIndex` stores references and
an omission count in the host-owned checkpoint, with no copied rows or subjects.

<CodeFile path="examples/artifacts/retained-source-evidence.ts" region="mount-and-continue" title="Fresh authorization on every historical read" />

The mount adds `find_source_evidence` and `read_source_evidence`. Find uses exact
typed subject and optional exact operation/scope filters; separate observations
remain separate. Read accepts an issued receipt reference and an optional named
dataset, JSON-pointer path and page. A dataset reference is not a receipt.

## Prepare historical metadata before a turn

Opt in separately with `sourceEvidence.preparation.admit` to read retained
subjects before synchronous `.configure()` runs. A run's `aroundTurn` receives
`SourceEvidencePreparation`; `recent(SourceEvidenceRecentArgs)` returns a
`SourceEvidenceRecentResult` page of `SourceEvidenceMetadata`, or a fixed
unavailable result. Its `SourceEvidencePreparationContext` carries the current
identity, cancellation and redaction policy, with no fabricated tool call,
dispatch or artifact capability. Ordinary tool admission is unchanged.

<CodeFile path="examples/artifacts/retained-source-evidence.ts" region="prepare-metadata" title="Explicit metadata admission and preparation" />

Pages contain no scalars, dataset descriptors or rows, including at admission.
Every retained entry repeats current producer, native permission and preparation
privacy checks. `complete` describes only the bounded retained-index scan, not
all prior lookups or source completeness. Index order is historical observation
order; multiple subjects from one call can be ambiguous. `recordedAt` is retention
time, not collection time. A current provider catalog is read once per preparation
at iteration zero; it does not activate a skill or offer an executable tool.
The capability expires before `proceed` and at wrapper exit. Missing, expired,
foreign or denied sources cannot be recovered through raw artifact fallback.

## Read retained values through native tools
Array pages return exact values with `offset`, `shown`, `total` and optional
`nextOffset`; oversized rows are unavailable rather than silently shortened.
`SourceEvidenceFindArgs` and `SourceEvidenceReadArgs` describe those requests;
`SourceEvidenceLimits` bounds their resource use and retention.

With `.findings()` mounted, an unavailable `_findings.previous` ID still refuses
the entire proposed tool call before execution. Retained-source mounts add fixed
`recovery` data to that batch refusal: omit unavailable previous entries, and use
only unique executed `tool_result` IDs from the current request. Artifact receipt
references are different identities. When both native readers were offered,
`recovery.retainedSource` names their find/read route; read references come only
from `find_source_evidence.candidates[].ref`. Its fixed `unknownFilters: "omit"`
policy keeps unknown optional operation/scope filters out of the request rather
than guessing them. This offers a recovery path, not a
grant of access or a promise that evidence exists. It never triggers a fresh
source query. Answer and native-resume refusal/terminal decisions stay unchanged.

## Keep the limits with the evidence

All results are marked historical. `recordedAt` is the native store's retention
time, not source collection time. Source period is separate. Partial status and
visible coverage survive; record-only coverage fields do not become model data.
Missing status or coverage remains undeclared. A governed rewrite cannot restore
metadata that governance removed.

`find.complete` means only that this bounded index scan reached its end with no
known index omissions. Failed capture, expiry, denial or an unretained earlier
call can still leave historical gaps. `detail.complete` means this response
contains the entire retained rowset; it does not prove complete source inventory
or a complete answer. Apply your domain coverage rules to the receipt and rows.

Defaults are 32 retained references, 8 KiB per receipt, 32 candidates scanned,
12 KiB per whole response and a 5-second asynchronous deadline per operation.
Hard maxima are 128 references/scans, 32 KiB per receipt/response and 30 seconds.
Static capture accepts at most 8 datasets, 24 named fields and 1000 rows per dataset,
under at most 1 MiB of admitted materialized JSON; default capture is 20 rows/64 KiB.
Array pages contain at most 20 rows. Each page rereads the existing scoped store;
there is no payload cache or automatic source query/refresh. Expired, foreign,
revoked, missing or oversized reads return the same unavailable result.

Deadlines stop asynchronous waiting and prevent late index appends; they cannot
preempt synchronous JavaScript or roll back an already accepted artifact write.
Keep native checkpoints host-owned: structural validation does not authenticate
an arbitrary imported checkpoint. This feature neither selects a question's
target nor certifies a model answer. The deterministic runnable example uses
synthetic local rows and a scripted provider; it makes no live model call.
